correctness.rationale: Orthogonal duality preserves d and reduces nonsingletons to k≤n/2. If U=I⊕A and V=I⊕B, pair corresponding basis vectors in A and B, and add dim(I) independent directions outside U+V. The resulting graph-of-isomorphism subspace is disjoint from each and supplies 00. At d=1 a third line over the common hyperplane gives 11, while a different hyperplane in U plus a vector outside U+V gives 10 and, symmetrically, 01. At d=2 a direct sum of I and one basis vector from each side gives 11; for 10 use an outside vector when k≥3 or span(u,u'+v) when k=2, including n=4. Beyond d=2, a common neighbor violates the triangle inequality and every neighbor of one endpoint misses the other. All distance categories used in the EF strategy occur around each first vertex; compare equality and the distinct extension masks in the third round. This proves the same-class games, all four separations and the Rado statement. The Gaussian minima follow by duality, embedding at fixed k from ambient 2k, monotonicity in q, and [2k choose k]_2≤[2k+2 choose k+1]_2 by adjoining a fixed independent line. They are 35 and 1395. The independent replay branches/replay_02.py generated actual vector spans and checked every distinct pair (including all three masks at distance 3) in binary dimensions (2,2),(2,1),(4,2),(6,3) and ternary (4,2); this was corroboration only. The frozen code was read, not run.

value.rationale: This classifies all finite-field Grassmann adjacency graphs at a natural fixed logical depth. In particular one local extension description explains why all larger diameters, over all finite fields, have one rank-three theory even though they fail the random-graph test. This is useful beyond one-instance checking and is not a claim about full limit theory.
